chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Isma'il ibn Sa'd al-Ash'ari from al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the Takbir in the two Eid prayers. He said: 'The Takbir in the first [rak'ah] is seven Takbirs before the recitation, and in the second [rak'ah] five Takbirs after the recitation.'

For indeed these narrations are attributed to Taqiyyah because they came in agreement with the opinion of some of the Sunnis, since we have previously presented narrations that include and indicate that the Takbir is in the two rak'ahs together after the recitation, and there is no contradiction between the narrations, so it is necessary to attribute these to a type of Taqiyyah. And what confirms what we presented is the clarity of what was narrated:

key_terms.التَّقِيَّة: Taqiyyah, the practice of concealing one's beliefs or adopting a different ruling to avoid persecution or align with others
key_terms.التَّكْبِير: Takbir, the act of saying 'Allahu Akbar' (God is Greater)
key_terms.الْعَامَّة: The general public, often referring to Sunni Muslims in Shia texts
key_terms.الْعِيدَيْنِ: The two Eids (Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha)

ai.seo_question: How many Takbirs are recited in the Eid prayers according to Shia jurisprudence and why?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) specifies seven Takbirs before recitation in the first rak'ah and five after recitation in the second, a format often cited in Sunni tradition. Shaykh al-Tusi contextualizes this by attributing it to Taqiyyah, reconciling it with other Shia narrations that place all Takbirs after the recitation in both rak'ahs, thereby preserving the distinct Shia ritual practice while acknowledging the validity of the alternative form.
